title: McDonald's Drive-Through Takes Horrifying Turn
description:
Two shooting videos released today - both out of DC: https://youtu.be/Ma6GjR-shPo

MIDWEST SAFETY: Uncover. Inform. Empower.

Please consider JOINING for $1 a month. It *really* helps us do original reporting like this. 

MERCH! Midwest-Safety.com

CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Tips? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com. 

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to reqeust removal. Email: mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com

Cure the Streets typically partners with formerly incarcerated people to use their influence to intervene in neighborhood disputes. Robinson was one of those formerly incarcerated people. According to the Washington Post, Robinson played an integral role in the 2016 murder of Demetrius Medley. On the day of the funeral for Robinson's older brother, himself a victim of a gun murder, Robinson had a tense exchange with Medley who was from a rival neighborhood. Robinson then told another man from his neighborhood, Kevin Grover, to smoke him if he came back. Minutes later, Grover shot Medley twice in the chest. Robinson pled guilty in 2018 to assault with intent to kill and served five years in federal prison. He was released in 2022, and by April of 2024, He was working with the Cure the Streets program. He became well known in the D.C. community as a positive role model for kids and frequented outreach events with Cure the Streets. Residents were also on edge awaiting the sentencing of two D.C. police officers, one found guilty of second-degree murder and the other for obstruction of justice. On September 10th, Robinson's family agreed to release the body cam footage to the public, and that night, around 100 demonstrators gathered at the McDonald's where Robinson was shot. The demonstrations were largely peaceful, though at one point, police arrested several people for throwing bottles and rocks at officers. On January 15, 2025, the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Columbia announced that there was insufficient evidence to pursue charges against the two officers who shot Robinson and both returned to full active duty.
